description: Brussels I Recast contains Art.1 defining material scope — civil and commercial matters
Brussels I Recast contains Art.4 — general jurisdiction based on defendant's domicile
Brussels I Recast contains Art.7 — special jurisdiction for contracts and torts
Brussels I Recast contains Art.8 — jurisdiction over co-defendants and counterclaims
Brussels I Recast contains Arts.10-16 — protective jurisdiction for insurance matters
Brussels I Recast contains Arts.17-19 — protective jurisdiction for consumer contracts
Brussels I Recast contains Arts.20-23 — protective jurisdiction for employment contracts
Brussels I Recast contains Art.24 — exclusive jurisdiction for immovable property, companies, IP
Brussels I Recast contains Art.25 — prorogation of jurisdiction by choice of court agreement
Brussels I Recast contains Art.29 — lis pendens rules for parallel proceedings
Brussels I Recast contains Art.30 — rules for related actions in different Member States
Brussels I Recast contains Art.31(2) — anti-torpedo rule giving priority to chosen court
Brussels I Recast contains Art.35 — provisional and protective measures
Brussels I Recast contains Arts.36-38 — automatic recognition of judgments
Brussels I Recast contains Arts.39-44 — enforcement without exequatur
Brussels I Recast contains Art.45 — grounds for refusal of recognition or enforcement
Rome I contains Art.3 — party autonomy as primary choice of law rule
Rome I contains Art.4 — default applicable law rules in absence of choice

Rome I contains Art.8 — special choice of law rules for employment contracts
Rome I contains Art.9 — overriding mandatory provisions

Rome II contains Art.5 — special rules for product liability

Brussels I Recast is the primary instrument governing jurisdiction in EU civil and commercial matters
Art.29 Brussels I Recast implements the lis pendens rule for EU cross-border litigation
Art.31(2) modifies the lis pendens rule by giving priority to chosen court to counter torpedo tactics
Forum non conveniens is excluded within the Brussels I Recast system per CJEU Owusu v Jackson
Arts.39-44 implement the abolition of exequatur for judgments in civil and commercial matters
EEO Regulation was an early instrument abolishing exequatur for uncontested claims
Art.35 Brussels I Recast governs provisional and protective measures in cross-border disputes
Anti-suit injunctions are incompatible with the Brussels I Recast system per CJEU Turner v Grovit
EAPO is a specialised interim/protective measure for cross-border account preservation
Rome I determines the applicable law for contractual obligations in cross-border disputes
Rome II determines the applicable law for non-contractual obligations in cross-border disputes
Limitation periods for contractual claims governed by the applicable law under Rome I Art.12(1)(d)
Limitation periods for tort claims governed by the applicable law under Rome II Art.15(h)
Mediation Directive suspends limitation periods during mediation process
Brussels I Recast Art.25 (intra-EU) and Hague Convention (international) both enforce choice of court agreements
Hague Convention governs jurisdiction for exclusive choice of court agreements internationally
Consumer jurisdiction rules in Brussels I Recast align with consumer choice of law rules in Rome I
Employment jurisdiction rules in Brussels I Recast align with employment choice of law rules in Rome I
Regulation 2020/1784 implements the EU framework for cross-border service of documents
Proper service is prerequisite for enforcement — defective service is ground for refusal under Art.45(1)(b)
Directive 2020/1828 establishes the EU framework for collective consumer redress
ESCP judgments are directly enforceable across EU without exequatur
Enforceable European Orders for Payment circulate freely without exequatur
Brussels I Recast provides the framework for cross-border enforcement of judgments
ESCP Regulation establishes the small claims procedure steps
EAPO Regulation establishes the account preservation order procedure steps
EOP Regulation establishes the European Order for Payment procedure steps
CJEU is the ultimate interpreter of Brussels I Recast via preliminary references
CJEU is the ultimate interpreter of Rome I via preliminary references
CJEU is the ultimate interpreter of Rome II via preliminary references
EJN-civil facilitates practical cooperation in service of documents between Member States
EJN-civil facilitates practical cooperation in cross-border evidence taking
Evidence Regulation supports the Brussels I Recast system by enabling cross-border evidence taking
Mediation Directive offers an alternative dispute resolution path complementing the Brussels I litigation framework
Legal Aid Directive ensures access to justice in cross-border disputes under the Brussels I framework
Insolvency proceedings excluded from Brussels I Recast scope (Art.1(2)(b)) — governed by Insolvency Regulation
Art.7(1) special jurisdiction for contracts interacts with Rome I determination of applicable law for the contract
Art.7(2) special jurisdiction for torts interacts with Rome II determination of applicable law for the tort
Overriding mandatory provisions can override the otherwise applicable law identified under Rome I
Product liability special rule in Art.5 overrides the general lex loci damni rule in Art.4
Unfair competition special rule in Art.6 overrides the general tort rule in Art.4
Exclusive jurisdiction under Art.24 overrides the general domicile-based jurisdiction rule
Choice of court agreement under Art.25 generally overrides the default domicile rule
Consumer protective jurisdiction restricts the validity of pre-dispute choice of court agreements
Employment protective jurisdiction restricts the validity of pre-dispute choice of court agreements
Insurance protective jurisdiction restricts the validity of choice of court agreements against policyholders
EAPO provides a pre-enforcement preservation mechanism complementing the enforcement process
EEO Regulation provides an alternative enforcement pathway for uncontested claims alongside Brussels I Recast
ESCP provides a simplified procedure for small cross-border claims within the Brussels I framework
European Order for Payment provides a uniform payment order procedure within the Brussels I framework
Legal Aid Directive supports access to justice for consumers participating in cross-border collective redress
